# What Dynatrace tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789ABCDEF, which no real
# credential is. Both portions are written in uppercase letters and digits, so
# the run serves for both: once and a half over for the twenty-four characters of
# the public identifier, four times over for the sixty-four of the secret. With
# the six character prefix and the two full stops in front, a token comes to
# ninety-six.

patterns: dynatrace-token

# The prefix names the token type, and Dynatrace reads it as three characters,
# one letter and two digits rather than as a list. dt0c01 is what its API pages
# print, dt0s01 the token that authorizes account changes over SCIM, dt0s16 a
# platform token; dt0s17 opens a client identifier its OAuth page prints and its
# table of prefixes does not list, which is why the letter and the digits are
# read as classes. They are one pattern because every kind carries a sixty-four
# character secret the vendor says to treat like a password, so a caller with
# reason to redact any of them has the same reason for the rest.

case:     an api token in an environment assignment
in:       DT_API_TOKEN=dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      DT_API_TOKEN=«dynatrace-token»

case:     a token in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Api-Token dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      Authorization: Api-Token «dynatrace-token»

case:     an account api token
in:       dt0s01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»

case:     a platform token
in:       dt0s16.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»

case:     a prefix the published table does not list
in:       dt0s17.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»

case:     a token in the command line a request is made from
in:       curl -H 'Authorization: Api-Token dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF' https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/metrics
out:      curl -H 'Authorization: Api-Token «dynatrace-token»' https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/metrics

case:     the two tokens a deployment is configured with
in:       {"apiToken":"dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF","paasToken":"dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF"}
out:      {"apiToken":"«dynatrace-token»","paasToken":"«dynatrace-token»"}

# The alphabet both portions are written in: the uppercase letters and the
# digits, which is the class Dynatrace spells for each of them in the expression
# it publishes. The opening is read in lowercase, which is the case every prefix
# the vendor prints is written in, and the letter naming the type in either case,
# which is what the same expression admits. What the alphabet leaves out is
# everything else, so a run carrying a lowercase letter, a hyphen or a space is
# no token.

case:     a lowercase public portion
in:       dt0c01.0123456789abcdef01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.0123456789abcdef01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a lowercase secret
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase opening
in:       DT0C01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      DT0C01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     an uppercase letter naming the type
in:       dt0C01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»

case:     a secret carrying a hyphen
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF-123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF-123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a secret broken by a space
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF 123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF 123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

# The lengths either side of each count. Both are numbers Dynatrace states in
# prose and again in the expression it publishes, and both are used as counts
# rather than floors: a portion one character short is no token, and a secret one
# character long is a token and one character that belongs to no credential. The
# second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the match — a
# boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real token
# written against a character of the same class would come through whole.

case:     a public portion of twenty-four characters and a secret of sixty-four is a token
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»

case:     a public portion of twenty-three characters is not
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF0123456.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF0123456.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a secret of sixty-three characters is not
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDE
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDE

case:     a run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0
out:      «dynatrace-token»0

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       DT_API_TOKEN_dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      DT_API_TOKEN_«dynatrace-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xdt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      x«dynatrace-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF-suffix
out:      «dynatrace-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF.
out:      the token is «dynatrace-token».

# Two tokens written together. No token begins inside another: the two letters an
# opening starts with are lowercase and neither portion is written in lowercase
# at all, so no position inside a token opens a candidate, and inside a prefix
# the letter naming the type could be a d but a digit stands where the t would
# have to. So two tokens written with nothing between them are two values and
# both go, and an opening standing where a public portion would have to stand
# ends the candidate in front of it and opens the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEFdt0s16.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «dynatrace-token»«dynatrace-token»

case:     an opening written where a public portion would stand
in:       dt0c01.dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.«dynatrace-token»

# The token identifier, which is the prefix and the public portion together.
# Dynatrace states that it can be safely displayed in the UI and used for logging
# purposes, so it is not a value and nothing here redacts one — redacting it
# would take away the one part of a token a caller is meant to keep a log by.
# What the pattern asks for past it is the separator and the sixty-four
# characters of the secret.

case:     a token identifier on its own
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567

case:     a token identifier in a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="token used" token=dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="token used" token=dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567

# And what this pattern leaves alone besides. A digest is written in lowercase
# hexadecimal and carries no full stop, so neither it nor its uppercase form is
# read behind the prefix. The OAuth client secret is not read either: the client
# identifier Dynatrace prints carries an eight character public portion where a
# token's is twenty-four, and no source of the vendor's states a length for the
# credential built on one.

case:     a sha-256 behind the prefix
in:       dt0c01.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dt0c01.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an uppercase sha-256 behind the prefix
in:       dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     an oauth client secret, whose public portion is eight characters
in:       dt0s02.0123ABCD.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0s02.0123ABCD.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     the client identifier the oauth page prints
in:       client_id=dt0s17.0123ABCD
out:      client_id=dt0s17.0123ABCD

# The token format this one replaced, which Dynatrace says remains valid and
# publishes no shape for. There is no prefix to search for and no count to read,
# so the two cases here carry a value with no prefix at all, standing for that
# class rather than for anything published.

case:     a value with no prefix in an environment assignment
in:       DT_API_TOKEN=0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      DT_API_TOKEN=0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a value with no prefix in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Api-Token 0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      Authorization: Api-Token 0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

# And the shapes that miss the grammar somewhere else: the separators written as
# hyphens, an opening that is not this vendor's, and text nothing in this format
# reaches.

case:     hyphens where the separators stand
in:       dt0c01-0123456789ABCDEF01234567-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dt0c01-0123456789ABCDEF01234567-0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     a run of the right lengths opening with no prefix
in:       xx0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      xx0c01.0123456789ABCDEF01234567.0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/metrics
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://abc12345.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/metrics
